C-COMMONMARK-EMPHASIS.Name: CommonMark emphasis delimiter pairing: strong/em stop stealing closers from later pairs
C-COMMONMARK-EMPHASIS.Summary: Both inline emphasis code paths pair the first opening delimiter run with the first flanking-valid closing run they meet while scanning forward, instead of pairing each closer with the nearest eligible opener as CommonMark requires. When a paragraph contains three or more delimiter runs of one character and one opener's would-be closer is invalidated by flanking (a space before the closing **), that orphaned opener swallows the sentence and steals the closer of a later, perfectly clean pair. The owner-reported live case (2026-10-26, editor screenshot): `**Zero-shot **— модель получает только инструкцию. **One-shot** — инструкцию и один готовый пример.` renders as ONE giant bold span `Zero-shot **— … **One-shot` with two stray literal `**` inside it — the clean `**One-shot**` pair is destroyed — while GitHub on the same text renders `**One-shot**` bold and leaves only the typo's asterisks literal (verified via the GitHub Markdown API on 2026-10-26). This change adds one shared, self-contained pairing module implementing the CommonMark 0.31 delimiter-stack algorithm (run scan, flanking classification, nearest-eligible-opener matching with the multiple-of-3 rule and run splitting) and gates both existing emphasis dispatches through it: muya's own inline tokenizer (src/muya/lib/parser/index.js:194-224, regexes at rules.js:38-39) — the WYSIWYG editor view — and the vendored marked fork's inlineLexer (src/muya/lib/parser/marked/inlineLexer.js:229-246, regexes at marked/inlineRules.js:23-24) — HTML/PDF export and copy-as-HTML (consumers: src/muya/lib/utils/exportHtml.js:47,73 and src/muya/lib/contentState/copyCutCtrl.js:6,64,246). The gate keeps every existing local check (regex shape, isLengthEven, validateEmphasize with its rule-16 heuristic and rule-17 lowerPriority) and only adds a pairing decision; paragraphs with fewer than three same-character delimiter runs take a zero-work fast path and tokenize byte-identically to today, which keeps the C-24 inline-token and C-30 lexer golden churn limited to genuine pairing-theft cases and keeps the C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 performance territory untouched (one linear scan per emphasis-bearing string, no re-lexing). Upstream context: the same bug class is marktext issue #2086, fixed upstream by PR #5555 (merged 2026-09-26, commit 18c724f9) with a new emphasis module — but upstream's muya has been restructured (packages/muya/src/inlineRenderer/emphasis.ts) and their rewrite does not map onto this tree's marked-fork architecture; per the owner instruction of 2026-10-27 ("do it, and you do not have to copy the example — a better own design is welcome"), this change implements the same algorithmic core (there is only one correct CommonMark pairing algorithm) as a surgical gate around the existing regexes rather than porting the upstream restructure.

Problem.Description: (1) The owner's document (2026-10-26 screenshot) shows the glossary paragraph rendering with a stray literal `**` before an em-dash and a broken `**One-shot` — one giant bold span. Deterministic reproduction through `tokenizer()` (2026-10-26, this repository): input `Хозяйке на заметку: **Zero-shot **— модель получает только инструкцию. **One-shot** — …` produces exactly one STRONG token with raw `**Zero-shot **— модель получает только инструкцию. **One-shot**` and children text `Zero-shot **— модель получает только инструкцию. **One-shot` — i.e. the typo'd opener at "Zero-shot" is left dangling by flanking rules (space before its `**`), the regex keeps scanning forward, and the `**` that should close "One-shot" is consumed as the giant span's closer, leaving the clean pair's own opening `**` as visible literal text. Italic has the same disease: `*Zero-shot *— модель. *One-shot*` produces one giant EM. (2) Root cause, muya path: the strong/em regexes `^(\*\*|__)(?=\S)([\s\S]*?[^\s\\])(\\*)\1(?!(\*|_))` / `^(\*|_)(?=\S)([\s\S]*?[^\s\*\\])(\\*)\1(?!\1)` (src/muya/lib/parser/rules.js:38-39) are non-greedy forward scans: first opener × first flanking-valid closer. `validateEmphasize` (src/muya/lib/parser/utils.js:154-180) checks per-run flanking (canOpenEmphasis/canCloseEmphasis, correct per CommonMark) and a rule-16 approximation, but nothing decides WHO a closer belongs to. (3) Root cause, export path: the marked fork's inlineLexer dispatch (marked/inlineLexer.js:229-246) uses the same first-closer grammar (marked/inlineRules.js:23-24) with the same shared validateEmphasize — so HTML export, print/PDF and copy-as-HTML render the same giant bold span; fixing only the editor would create an editor-vs-export inconsistency worse than today's uniform wrongness. (4) CommonMark requires the delimiter-stack algorithm: process closers left to right, each closer pairs with the nearest eligible opener on the stack (multiple-of-3 rule for mixed runs), consumed runs split. GitHub anchors verified via the GitHub Markdown API on 2026-10-26: the report paragraph → typo asterisks literal + `One-shot` bold; `**a **b** c**` → everything one bold span (`a b c`); `*foo **bar* baz**` → triple-nested em (the mod-3 case — which proves a naive "reject if any can-open run sits between" guard would REGRESS inputs muya currently gets right; the full stack algorithm is required). (5) The parse change is deliberately guarded: tests/renderer/muya/inline-token-parity.test.js (C-24) and lexer-token-parity.test.js (C-30) pin tokenizer output byte-for-byte with UPDATE_*_GOLDENS escape hatches that exist exactly for intended parse changes; this change uses that flow and reviews the diff.

Goals.R-1: New governed module `src/muya/lib/parser/emphasisPairing.js` (inside M-012 muya, no new graph anchor): (a) `scanDelimiterRuns(src)` — every maximal `*`/`_` run with start/end/char/length plus CommonMark flanking classification (left/right-flanking, can-open/can-close, intraword-`_` restrictions) computed on the raw character stream, BOF/EOF treated as whitespace, punctuation per the shared PUNCTUATION_REG (src/muya/lib/parser/utils.js:4) and whitespace per a single-character test; runs preceded by an odd number of backslashes (escapes) and runs inside inline-code spans (the existing code-span grammar, single shared source) are masked out because tighter constructs own those characters; (b) `computeEmphasisPairing(src)` — the CommonMark 0.31 process-emphasis algorithm over the masked runs (closers left-to-right, nearest eligible opener, multiple-of-3 rule with the both-multiples-of-3 exception, delimiter consumption from the inner ends of runs, run splitting with leftovers re-usable, openers between a matched pair removed per the spec), returning an ordered list of matches {openerSegStart/openerSegEnd, closerSegStart/closerSegEnd, type strong|em} plus a lookup by absolute position; self-contained, no dependency on the tokenizer, O(runs) time, one pass, no allocation beyond the run list; exposes a test-only activation counter (reset + read) so the fast path can be pinned.
Goals.R-2: Fast path with zero behavior change: `computeEmphasisPairing` returns null (and increments no activation counter) unless, after masking, some delimiter character either carries ≥3 usable runs (the theft shape) or has a single run of length ≥3 (the run-splitting shape — `***`), while at least one run can open and at least one later run can close; everything else tokenizes byte-identically to today (no gate call effect). This is what keeps the golden churn surgical and the C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 perf territory untouched: ordinary prose with 0–2 runs of length ≤2 never pays for the scan beyond the cheap run-count check. Calibration recorded at plan time: a paragraph with one bold pair AND one italic pair has four asterisk runs and does activate (one linear scan, output unchanged — counter-pinned); the zero-activation pin is a single-pair paragraph.
Goals.R-3: Gate in muya's tokenizer (src/muya/lib/parser/index.js strong|em dispatch, lines 194-224): the per-invocation pairing is computed lazily once (memoized local, on the level's full source string; recursive child invocations compute their own — correct, since pairing is per-string). A regex match at absolute [start,end) with marker length L is accepted only if the pairing contains a match whose opener segment starts at start, whose closer segment ends at end, and both segments have length L. When the regex match is rejected, a bounded retry runs: if a pairing match has its opener segment starting at the current position, build the token for exactly [start, closerSegEnd) with marker length = opener segment length, apply the SAME existing local checks the regex path applies (content shape approximated by today's constraints, isLengthEven on the backlash group, validateEmphasize including rule-16 and rule-17 lowerPriority) and emit strong/em accordingly; on any failure fall through to literal text one character at a time, exactly as today. Token shapes, ranges, marker/children/backlash fields, and the recursive children lexing stay exactly as the current code produces them — the gate changes only WHICH spans win.
Goals.R-4: Same gate in the marked fork (marked/inlineLexer.js strong/em dispatch): compute the pairing once per output() level on the level's full source, track the absolute offset as levelSrc.length − src.length, and apply the identical two-step gate after the existing validateEmphasize. Export/copy therefore renders the same spans as the editor for every input where the two paths agree today; the report paragraph becomes consistent (One-shot bold) on both surfaces.
Goals.R-5: Deliberate golden recapture: run UPDATE_INLINE_GOLDENS=1 and UPDATE_LEXER_GOLDENS=1 (the flow writes then fails on purpose — run on the pre-change lexer capture is NOT the case here: this IS an intended parse change), inspect the golden diff, and record in the plan that every changed digest is a theft-class or run-splitting improvement, not collateral. The C-24 STRESS corpus gains the owner-report sentence and upstream's `*a *b* c*` / `**a **b** c**` probes so the pairing class stays pinned forever.
Goals.R-6: Verification: a new suite `tests/renderer/muya/emphasis-pairing.test.js` pins (a) the owner-report paragraph verbatim → one STRONG `**One-shot**`, zero stray asterisks inside it, the typo `**` pairs literal (same assertion for the italic twin); (b) GitHub-anchored expectations for the theft class (report case, `**a **b** c**`, `A **B **— C** D`, `x **b **— c **d** e`); (c) the mod-3 corner `*foo **bar* baz**` documents this implementation's tree (no giant-span regression, behavior recorded as a pin, not claimed as cmark-identical); (d) `***bold italic***` improves from today's strong[em]+stray to em[strong]; (e) masking: `\*` escapes and `` *a `*` b* `` code spans never produce delimiter runs; (f) parity — for every corpus input the muya tokenizer's strong/em spans equal the marked fork renderer's on the same string; (g) fast path — the activation counter stays zero for a paragraph with two runs and one for the report paragraph; (h) generator round-trip: token raws re-serialize to the input. Existing suites (markdown-round-trip, pele-*, export-*, copy-data, edit-preview-flow) stay green.
Goals.R-7: Governance: MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY in the new module and both dispatch files; M-012 graph narrative delta and V-M-012 verification delta in the same bundle as the code (new commands and the golden-recapture note); grace lint --assertions current shows no new findings beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline; observed-write overlaps with active changes (C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 owns large-doc perf behavior in the same files' neighborhood; C-GITHUB-THEME and C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT consume export output) are checked with grace lint --parallel-preflight before the first write.
Goals.R-8: Owner approval recorded: the owner approved execution by chat instruction on 2026-10-27 ("делай, тем более есть пример (но не обязательно копировать может лучше придумаешь)" — "do it, especially since there is an example (but copying is not required — coming up with something better is welcome)") after reviewing the 2026-10-26 diagnosis (screenshot analysis, tokenizer reproduction, GitHub anchor, upstream PR #5555 context). This approval covers the spec and the implementation; release/train admission remains a separate owner instruction.

Constraints.Item: Language: every committed artifact of this change is English; the owner's Russian report sentence appears in tests only as product fixture data (like the existing RU fixtures in the corpus), and the owner quote above is translated with the original kept for traceability.

No grammar rewrite: the existing regexes, validateEmphasize, lowerPriority and rule-16 heuristic stay in place; the pairing module decides only WHICH regex-visible candidate span wins. Any case the pairing cannot decide falls back to today's behavior, never to an exception.

Full CommonMark compliance of emphasis is explicitly out of scope: known remaining deviations (link-text delimiters joining the stack across bracket boundaries, marked's code-span precedence order, cmark's exact rendering of mod-3 corners) are documented as pins in the suite, not chased.

Performance is a first-class gate: one linear scan per string, no regex backtracking beyond the existing rules, no re-lexing, no new per-character work; paragraphs under the R-2 threshold must show zero pairing activations (counter-pinned). C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0's fixtures and gates must stay green and unchanged.

The C-24/C-30 golden update uses the UPDATE_*_GOLDENS=1 escape hatches exactly as designed for intended parse changes; the resulting diff is reviewed and summarized in the plan's review pass (every changed digest must be attributable to the pairing class).

Token shapes and ranges are load-bearing for the WYSIWYG (cursor math, contentState formats, highlights): the gate may change WHICH spans become strong/em but must not change the shape of the tokens it emits (same fields as today) nor any range bookkeeping convention.
Existing gates stay green and unweakened: npm test, the muya suites, e2e; grace lint --assertions current shows no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline.
No release or train admission follows from this approval; version bumps, tags and store uploads stay behind their separate owner release instruction.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Porting upstream PR #5555's restructured inlineRenderer/emphasis.ts onto this tree (wrong architecture shape; only the algorithmic idea is shared).
Fixing link-vs-emphasis precedence, image alt emphasis, or marked's code-span-after-strong rule order; html escaping; any block-level parsing.
Changing the WYSIWYG emphasis toolbar behavior, format painting, or how markdown is re-serialized (generator untouched).
UI, locales, themes, or release materials; any Rust-side change.
Matching cmark byte-for-byte on every CommonMark spec example (the suite pins this implementation's actual trees for corners; GitHub parity is asserted only for the theft class).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The owner-report paragraph (both the bold original and its italic twin) tokenizes to literal typo asterisks plus exactly one clean emphasis token around the later pair (`**One-shot**` / `*One-shot*`), with no token containing a stray `**` inside emphasis, and the same paragraph exported through the marked fork renders `One-shot` bold with the typo asterisks literal — editor and export agree.

Theft class fixed: `**a **b** c**`, `A **B **— C** D`, `x **b **— c **d** e` and `*a *b* c*` no longer produce a span that swallows a later clean pair's opener or leaves its closer stolen; each renders per the GitHub anchors recorded in this spec.

No collateral: inputs without the ≥3-run theft shape tokenize byte-identically to the pre-change tokenizer — pinned by the C-24/C-30 golden diff being empty except for digest entries attributable to the pairing class (each listed in the plan), and by a fast-path counter test (0 activations for a two-run paragraph, 1 for the report paragraph).

Corners pinned: `*foo **bar* baz**` does not regress (no giant span; the recorded tree stays), `***bold italic***` improves to em[strong] (no stray literal `*`), `\*`-escaped and code-span-masked runs never pair, intraword `snake_case_word` stays plain, and generator(tokens) round-trips every suite input.
Parity: for every input in the new suite and the extended STRESS corpus, muya tokenizer strong/em spans equal marked-fork renderer strong/em spans on the same string.

Governance: MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated in emphasisPairing.js, parser/index.js, parser/rules.js (if touched), marked/inlineLexer.js; M-012/V-M-012 deltas routed in the same bundle; npm test green (muya suites, renderer suites, whatsNew untouched); grace lint --assertions current no new findings; two consecutive clean four-corner review passes recorded in the plan.
